rationale: X explains the requested Persistence, Dirty, scoping, query-cache, association-cache, and edge-case behavior very well, but it contains two concrete implementation-flow errors the references avoid. It says reload does not allocate a new record even though _find_record/find_by! instantiates fresh_object, whose attributes and association cache are then transferred, and it places Aggregations inside AutosaveAssociation in the call chain even though a class using composed_of has Aggregations ahead of AutosaveAssociation in its ancestors. Because the scenario explicitly asks for implementation and control flow and object identity versus replaced internal state, these errors keep X below reference parity despite the otherwise strong walkthrough.

shortcomings.summary: Incorrectly denies allocation of the fresh database record.
shortcomings.evidence: X opens with 'It does not allocate a new record,' but Persistence#reload assigns fresh_object from _find_record/find_by!, then steals fresh_object's @attributes and @association_cache; X later acknowledges that discarded fresh_object, creating an internal contradiction.

shortcomings.summary: Orders the optional Aggregations reload wrapper incorrectly.
shortcomings.evidence: X diagrams AutosaveAssociation#reload calling Aggregations#reload, but composed_of includes ActiveRecord::Aggregations in the model subclass, producing ancestor order Aggregations, AutosaveAssociation, AttributeMethods::Dirty, Persistence; aggregation-cache clearing therefore occurs before the Autosave wrapper.

strengths.summary: Core Persistence and Dirty behavior is accurately traced.
strengths.evidence: X correctly explains query-cache clearing, _find_record, find_by! failure before the persistence swap, transfer and owner rebinding of the fresh association cache, replacement of @attributes, persistence flags, and post-super mutation-tracker reset.

strengths.summary: Scoped and unscoped reload semantics are comprehensive.
strengths.evidence: It correctly distinguishes ordinary default scopes, all_queries default scopes, reload(unscoped: true), ordinary relation scoping, scoping(all_queries: true), query constraints, and RecordNotFound outcomes.

strengths.summary: All requested observable edge cases are answered with query, raise, identity, and state effects.
strengths.evidence: X covers unsaved changes, saved_changes reset, default-scope visibility, deleted rows, and stale loaded associations, including the strict-loading preload exception and next-access association query.
